bayts.text: he is like one who was present on the day of Ḥunayn and stood firm, and on the day of Badr, and aided the best of creation, he who gives understanding.
Whoever honours the birth of our Prophet, Gate of Guidance, will not be called to account tomorrow, at the Reckoning that silences.
Whoever has taken part in (the celebration of) the birth of the best of creation, honouring it, joyful, with sugar or with meat,
he has attained what makes joy everlasting, and will meet no harm on the Day the communities are gathered.
Whoever has prepared food for those who recited (the Mawlid) in his honour, with veneration, has stored up the treasures of the people of lofty aspiration.
And whoever has recited over something (the account of) the birth of the master of creation, to draw blessing from it, will see it grow in abundance.
And if (the account of) the birth of the best of mankind is recited over water, drinking it, by (the grace of) the Purified one, restrains the scheming of the humbled (foe).
Drinking that water illumines the heart, by (the grace of) the Answered one, revives the heart without flaw, and keeps one from wretchedness.
Celebrating the birth of the Bearer of glad tidings (Muḥammad) protects the family and the dwellings; in it is healing for the breasts, for every rightly guided one who belongs to him.
May the Everlasting (Allah), who makes my joy endure, bless the best of mankind, with the Family and the Companions, precious pearls, with a peace that enfolds them.
O Inspirer, who granted success, bless him who was created and surpassed creation in character as in form, and grant peace.
He was of middle stature, of noble and clear bearing; he was not excessive (in height), nor was he dark of complexion.
He was not corpulent, nor round and full of face; rather he surpassed all who rose among the descendants of Adam.
He stood taller than whoever walked beside him, at any time; he was generous and hospitable of soul, and he laughed by smiling.
He was majestic, of lively countenance, his whiteness tinged with red, long-lashed, large-eyed, of noble figure.
He smiled the most radiant of smiles, like lightning or like hailstones; and his laughter dispelled the darkness, like lamps in the gloom.
His face was round, he was slender, luminous, splendid, of amber complexion, and he spoke in measured cadence.
It was as though water of gold flowed upon his refined cheek; his limbs were slender and his nose of noble height.
Perfect of ear, deep-black of eye, with bright and slightly parted teeth, eyes veined with red, radiant; his face erased every sorrow.
He is the most perfect of creatures, manifest in form and in character; never has his like been seen in virtues, nor ever will be.
Our Aḥmad, our mercy, our Ḥāmid, our blessing, our Maḥmūd, our joy; and his generosity puts the rains to shame.
Truly I address the Beautiful (Allah), invoking blessing upon the Messenger and greeting with peace him who unites his company (with God), in my words.
Bless the Cloaked One (Al-Muddaththir, Muḥammad), the best of creatures, the Bearer of glad tidings, effacer of falsehood, the Purified, and his Family, and grant peace.
Bless the Enwrapped One (Al-Muzzammil, Muḥammad), dispeller of darkness, the Hoped-for, who pours his bounty on the needy, and his Companions, and grant peace.
Bless the Servant of God, His Beloved, the Remembrance of God, His Elect, the Sword of God, and his Family, and grant peace.
Bless the Company of God, His gift, the Gate of God, His Path, the Guidance of God, and his Companions, and grant peace.
Bless our master, our patron, our exemplary Guide, our beloved, our intercessor, and his Family, and grant peace.
Bless him who was educated (by God), possessor of sanctity, the educator, the best of Messengers and Prophets, and his Companions, and grant peace.
Bless the Gate of Bliss, the Straight Path (aṣ-Ṣirāṭ al-Mustaqīm), Muḥammad, the best of beings, and his Family, and grant peace.
Bless the glory of the Arabs: he removes distress, he raises ranks; and his Companions, and grant peace.
Bless the Effacer (Al-Māḥī), the Trustee, the one who relies (on God), the Guarantor, our guide to the Path, and his Family, and grant peace.
Bless the sea of seas, the lion against the foes, the healing of breasts, banisher of wretchedness, full moon of full moons, and his Companions, and grant peace.
He is the one who has led munificence to whoever comes asking for gifts; and whoever heads towards him in aggression meets ruin in terror.
He is the one through whom my hand reached out to my Lord, the Most Bountiful, and He gave me the best, without "give me" or "how much?".
His are wonders that came to no predecessor and that no successor can equal, by the grace of Him (Allah) who grants precedence.
Among them, the stone's greeting to him, the walking of the tree, the splitting of the moon for him, by (the will of) Him who possesses Permanence and Eternity.
The cloud gave him shade; he saw behind him as before him; his eyes would sleep, but his heart did not sleep.
Among them, flies avoiding his body and his garments; and likewise the easing of difficulties, by (the grace of) God, Giver of spoils.
Among them, the birds seeking intercession through him, the camel that complained to him, and the pure water that gushed from the hand of the Generous one.
The glorification (tasbīḥ) of food was heard in the palm of the best of mankind; the speech of a gazelle in words: a miracle of the Revered.
The speech of a lizard has come down among them in an established text; the moaning of a trunk has come down among the wonders of the Honoured.
Riḍwān (the keeper of Paradise) would visit his dwelling to honour him; among them (the wonders), the birds sent against the arrogant,
(when) he (Abraha) set out for the Sacred House (the Kaʿba) to demolish it, one among men led on by degrees to ruin, through his ignorance of the Magnified one.
And God, exalted, did to his army what He did, by the rank of him (Muḥammad), and made their scheme vain (casting it) into the sea.
Each of the arrogant died by the most baleful of stones: the Lord of mankind made them like morsels for a glutton.
And among the wonders appeared what the cave of the Exemplar (Muḥammad, the cave of Thawr) held; may He (Allah) who through him guided those of understanding send blessing upon him:
a spider that wove (its web) and a dove that settled (there), hovering, and thereby they hid those two (the Prophet and Abū Bakr) as under a veil of darkness.
The disbelievers came and followed the tracks of the Effacer (Al-Māḥī, Muḥammad), but saw nothing of him, and returned in pain.
He was concealed, together with the greatest Freed One (Abū Bakr), in the cave, within sight of their very gazes, and they saw no one.
The protection of the Guardian (Al-Ḥafīẓ), the Defender (Al-Māniʿ), makes weapons needless for every humble servant who seeks the best of sanctuaries.
